question: How much will Crude Oil Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 23 - Dec 4)

calls.reasoning: Two-week CL minus ES return difference; status quo centred near zero. The spread is dominated by oil's high-volatility 2026 regime: OVX ~52 on Nov 12 (52-week range 28-126), with WTI near $88.6 after two weekly declines on easing Middle East tension and an emerging supply surplus. S&P sold off about 1% on Nov 16 on AI/tech worries, with energy the only gaining sector. Slight negative median shift for a possible Dec-to-Jan front-month roll near the P0 date in a downward-sloping (backwardated) curve, plus surplus momentum. Fat tails priced via small escape masses: a geopolitical spike on the upside, a peace-plus-glut crash on the downside. Market check: Kalshi has only a WTI end-of-year max-price contract (not matching); Polymarket and Manifold have nothing; no matching market found.

On Nov 16 WTI was about $87, down ~12% over the month: the IEA now projects a Q4 surplus of 1.7 mb/d, Hormuz exports are recovering, SPR releases are running and Chinese demand is soft. At the same time, tanker mine strikes and Iran attacks keep upside tail risk alive. OVX sits around 52 (52-week range 28-126). Thanksgiving shortens the window to about 9.5 sessions. Escape mass outside ±25 is small but real: a Hormuz escalation on the upside, a US-Iran settlement or price collapse on the downside.
